You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Salt Reed broadcast","question":"What claims can the archivist put in the tape catalogue?","claims":{"A":"Staff digitised the master tape on Friday.","B":"The original tape casing is labelled programme SR-63.","C":"The master tape contains more than 30 minutes of programme audio."},"sources":{"S1":"transfer log records the master tape digitised Friday.","S2":"the programme grid allocates 35 minutes. Engineers routinely removed news and announcements from masters, so the slot is only an estimate.","S3":"tape casing is labelled programme SR-36 by the original studio."},"follow_up":{"S4":"independent digital preservation report distinguishes programme audio from silence and assigns the master 28 minutes of programme audio."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"supported","citations":["S1"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S3"],"confidence":95},"C":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S4"],"confidence":85}},"note":"Claim A is supported by the transfer log (S1) explicitly stating the master tape was digitised on Friday. Claim B is contradicted by the tape casing label (S3) which shows SR-36, not SR-63. Claim C is contradicted by the independent preservation report (S4) which measures 28 minutes of programme audio, less than 30 minutes; the programme grid (S2) only estimates 35 minutes but is not definitive."}

parsed.note: Claim A is supported by the transfer log (S1) explicitly stating the master tape was digitised on Friday. Claim B is contradicted by the tape casing label (S3) which shows SR-36, not SR-63. Claim C is contradicted by the independent preservation report (S4) which measures 28 minutes of programme audio, less than 30 minutes; the programme grid (S2) only estimates 35 minutes but is not definitive.
